title: Formal fibres of a polynomial ring over a complete local ring at a maximal ideal over the closed point
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is complete, i.e. $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] (the canonical map to $\varprojlim_nS/\mathfrak n^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is bijective), let $S[x]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable over $S$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and let $\mathfrak Q\subset S[x]$ be a maximal ideal with $\mathfrak Q\cap S=\mathfrak n$. Let $S[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$ be the localization of $S[x]$ at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(S[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS[x]_{\mathfrak Q}/\mathfrak Q^nS[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$ its completion at its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then the canonical map $S[x]_{\mathfrak Q}\to(S[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge$ is a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; equivalently (it is flat with Noetherian fibre rings, the source being Noetherian), for every prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ of $S[x]$ the formal fibre $(S[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge\otimes_{S[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring), paragraphs 2-5 (lines 12596-12637): 'Let R be a Noetherian complete local ring and let q in R[x] be a maximal ideal lying over the maximal ideal of R ...'; that argument uses Lemma 07PN (lemma-check-G-ring-easy), Lemma 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite), Algebra Lemma 032D (lemma-complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular), Algebra Lemma 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up), Lemma 07NY (lemma-completion-regular), Lemma 07PR (lemma-helper-G-ring) and Lemma 07PU (lemma-another-helper-G-ring). No tag of its own: it is the 'right vertical arrow' step of 07PV, stated here as a node.

proof.text: (Flatness, Noetherian fibres, reduction to the formal fibres.) Put $T=S[x]_{\mathfrak Q}$ and $C=T^\wedge$. $S[x]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], hence so is its localization $T$ (every ideal of $T$ is extended from an ideal of $S[x]$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak QT$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. So $T\to C$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], $C$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and every fibre ring $C\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak s)$, $\mathfrak s$ a prime of $T$, is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian]. The primes of $T$ are the $\mathfrak rT$ with $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ a prime of $S[x]$, and $\kappa(\mathfrak rT)=\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ as $T$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; for $T$-modules $M,N$ one has $M\otimes_{S[x]}N=M\otimes_TN$ (for $u\notin\mathfrak Q$: $mu^{-1}\otimes n=mu^{-1}\otimes uu^{-1}n=m\otimes u^{-1}n$), so $C\otimes_T\kappa(\mathfrak rT)=C\otimes_{S[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$. By the definition of a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] it remains to show: for every prime $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ of $S[x]$ the $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$-algebra $C\otimes_{S[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV (proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring), second paragraph, lines 12596-12602 ('Let r subset q be a prime ideal. We want to show that R[x]_q^ (x)_{R[x]} kappa(r) is a geometrically regular algebra over kappa(r)'); flatness of the completion and Noetherian fibres (Definition 07BZ of a regular ring map) written out

proof.text: (Reduction to a complete local domain.) Fix $\mathfrak r$. Let $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak r\cap S$, a prime of $S$ contained in $\mathfrak Q\cap S=\mathfrak n$, $A=S/\mathfrak p$, and $\pi:S[x]\to A[x]$ the map reducing coefficients mod $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]: it is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak pS[x]$ (a polynomial maps to $0$ iff all its coefficients lie in $\mathfrak p$). By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] $A$ is a Noetherian local ring, complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak p$, and it is a domain. As $\mathfrak pS[x]\subseteq\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak Q$, $\bar{\mathfrak Q}=\pi(\mathfrak Q)$ and $\bar{\mathfrak r}=\pi(\mathfrak r)$ are primes of $A[x]$ with $\pi^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak Q})=\mathfrak Q$, $\pi^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak r})=\mathfrak r$; $A[x]/\bar{\mathfrak Q}\cong S[x]/\mathfrak Q$ is a field, so $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$ is maximal; $\bar{\mathfrak Q}\cap A=(\mathfrak Q\cap S)/\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_A$ and $\bar{\mathfrak r}\cap A=(\mathfrak r\cap S)/\mathfrak p=(0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] (with $I=\mathfrak pS[x]$) the map $\lambda:T\to A[x]_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak pT$, and it maps the maximal ideal $\mathfrak QT$ onto the maximal ideal of $A[x]_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}}$; the same lemma at $\mathfrak r$ gives $A[x]_{\bar{\mathfrak r}}\cong S[x]_{\mathfrak r}/\mathfrak pS[x]_{\mathfrak r}$, and dividing by the maximal ideals (note $\mathfrak pS[x]_{\mathfrak r}\subseteq\mathfrak rS[x]_{\mathfrak r}$) an isomorphism of $S[x]$-algebras $\kappa(\mathfrak r)\cong\kappa(\bar{\mathfrak r})$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-quotient] applied to the Noetherian local ring $T$ (Step 1) and $\lambda$, $(A[x]_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}})^\wedge\cong C/\mathfrak pC$ compatibly with the maps from $S[x]$. Since $\mathfrak p$ annihilates $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, we get isomorphisms of $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$-algebras $(A[x]_{\bar{\mathfrak Q}})^\wedge\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\bar{\mathfrak r})\cong(C/\mathfrak pC)\otimes_{S[x]/\mathfrak pS[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)\cong C\otimes_{S[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$, and geometric regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] only depends on the algebra up to isomorphism. So it suffices to prove: $(\dagger)$ if $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ is a Noetherian local domain which is $\mathfrak m_A$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $\mathfrak Q\subset A[x]$ a maximal ideal with $\mathfrak Q\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$ and $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ a prime with $\mathfrak r\cap A=(0)$, then $(A[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge\otimes_{A[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV, second paragraph, lines 12602-12607 ('Set p = R cap r. Then we can replace R by R/p and q and r by their images in R/p[x], see Lemma 07PN. Hence we may assume that R is a domain and that r cap R = (0)'); the identity used is the one in the proof of Lemma Tag 07PN (lemma-check-G-ring-easy, line 12194), here for the ideal pS[x] contained in r, written out with Algebra Lemma Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and Proposition 00CT; quotient: Algebra Lemma Tag 0325

proof.text: (Passing to a regular subring.) Let $A,\mathfrak Q,\mathfrak r$ be as in $(\dagger)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-domain-finite-over-regular] there is a subring $A_0\subseteq A$ which is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (in particular a Noetherian domain), complete with respect to $\mathfrak m_0=\mathfrak m_A\cap A_0$, such that $A=\sum_{i=1}^sA_0a_i$ is a finitely generated $A_0$-module, and $A_0\cong k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a field $k$ or $A_0\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$. Then $A_0[x]\subseteq A[x]$ and $A[x]=\sum_iA_0[x]a_i$ is a finite $A_0[x]$-module, in particular a finitely generated $A_0[x]$-algebra; $A_0[x]$ and $A[x]$ are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $\mathfrak Q_0=\mathfrak Q\cap A_0[x]$ and $\mathfrak r_0=\mathfrak r\cap A_0[x]$: primes with $\mathfrak r_0\subseteq\mathfrak Q_0$, $\mathfrak Q_0\cap A_0=\mathfrak m_A\cap A_0=\mathfrak m_0$ and $\mathfrak r_0\cap A_0=(0)$. $\mathfrak Q_0$ is maximal: $D=A_0[x]/\mathfrak Q_0$ is a subring of the field $L=A[x]/\mathfrak Q$, which is a finite $D$-module, hence integral over $D$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; for $0\ne y\in D$ the element $y^{-1}\in L$ satisfies $y^{-n}+d_1y^{-n+1}+\dots+d_n=0$ with $d_j\in D$, and multiplying by $y^{n-1}$ gives $y^{-1}=-(d_1+d_2y+\dots+d_ny^{n-1})\in D$. The map $A_0[x]\to A[x]$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak Q$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]: the fibre ring $F=A[x]\otimes_{A_0[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak Q_0)$ is spanned over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak Q_0)$ by the images of $a_1,\ldots,a_s$, so $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak Q_0)}F<\infty$; for each prime $P$ of $F$ the domain $F/P$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(\mathfrak Q_0)$-algebra, hence a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective), so every prime of $F$ is maximal; distinct maximal ideals $P_1,\ldots,P_t$ give a surjection $F\to\prod_iF/P_i$ (Chinese remainder theorem), so $t\le\dim F$; thus $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is finite with all points closed, hence discrete, and the point of $\mathfrak Q$ is isolated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-quasi-finite-ascent] to $R=A_0[x]$, $R'=A[x]$ and the primes $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak Q$ of $A[x]$, lying over $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak r_0\subseteq\mathfrak p=\mathfrak Q_0$: if $(\ddagger)$ the $\kappa(\mathfrak r_0)$-algebra $(A_0[x]_{\mathfrak Q_0})^\wedge\otimes_{A_0[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r_0)$ is geometrically regular over $\kappa(\mathfrak r_0)$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], then $(\dagger)$ holds. So it suffices to prove $(\ddagger)$ for the regular complete local domain $A_0$, the maximal ideal $\mathfrak Q_0$ of $A_0[x]$ over $\mathfrak m_0$ and the prime $\mathfrak r_0\subseteq\mathfrak Q_0$ with $\mathfrak r_0\cap A_0=(0)$. Let $K_0=(A_0)_{(0)}$ be the fraction field of $A_0$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV, third paragraph, lines 12609-12615 ('By Algebra, Lemma 032D we can find R_0 subset R which is regular and such that R is finite over R_0. Applying Lemma 07PP we see that it suffices to prove ... when, in addition to the above, R is a regular complete local ring'); Algebra Lemma Tag 032D (line 45065); More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PP (lemma-G-ring-goes-up-quasi-finite, line 12214), item (1); finite implies quasi-finite (Algebra 00PL, 00PM) and maximality of Q_0 written out

proof.text: (The completion is regular.) Put $C_0=(A_0[x]_{\mathfrak Q_0})^\wedge$. The regular local ring $A_0$ is a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $A_0\to A_0[x]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] (case $n=1$), so $A_0[x]$ is a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] and $A_0[x]_{\mathfrak Q_0}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its completion $C_0$ is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] which is regular local [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], hence a regular ring [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization]. Consequently, for every multiplicative subset $V\subseteq A_0[x]$, the ring $V^{-1}C_0=C_0\otimes_{A_0[x]}V^{-1}A_0[x]$ (localization at the image of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]) is a regular ring: it is Noetherian (its ideals are extended from $C_0$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), its primes are the $V^{-1}P$ with $P$ a prime of $C_0$ not meeting the image of $V$, and $(V^{-1}C_0)_{V^{-1}P}\cong(C_0)_P$ is a regular local ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07PV, fourth paragraph, lines 12617-12626 ('Since R is regular the ring R[x] is regular (Algebra, Lemma 07NF). Hence the localization R[x]_q is regular. Hence the completions R[x]_q^ are regular, see Lemma 07NY'); Algebra Lemma Tag 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up, line 46610), Algebra Lemma Tag 0AFS (line 27126), More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07NY (line 10668); smoothness of R -> R[x]: Algebra Definition 00T6 and Lemma 00T7

proof.text: (Characteristic $0$, $\mathfrak r_0=(0)$.) Suppose $\mathfrak r_0=(0)$. $A_0[x]$ is a domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], so with $V=A_0[x]\setminus\{0\}$ we have $\kappa((0))=V^{-1}A_0[x]$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and the fibre is $C_0\otimes_{A_0[x]}\kappa((0))=V^{-1}C_0$, a regular ring by Step 4. If moreover $K_0$ has characteristic $0$, so does $\kappa((0))\supseteq K_0$, whose only finite purely inseparable extension is itself [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; hence the fibre is geometrically regular over $\kappa((0))$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], which is $(\ddagger)$ in this case.

Since $\mathfrak r_0\cap W=\emptyset$, $\mathfrak r_0K_0[x]$ is a nonzero prime of the principal ideal domain $K_0[x]$, hence $=fK_0[x]$ with $f$ irreducible of degree $\ge1$, maximal, and $\mathfrak r_0K_0[x]\cap A_0[x]=\mathfrak r_0$; clearing denominators we take $f\in\mathfrak r_0$. Let $\partial=d/dx$, a derivation of $A_0[x]$. It extends to $A_0[x]_{\mathfrak Q_0}$, then to its completion $C_0$ compatibly with $A_0[x]	o C_0$, then to $R=W^{-1}C_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends]; call the result $D$. Writing $\iota:A_0[x]	o R$ for the canonical map, the construction gives $D\circ\iota=\iota\circ\partial$; for $w\in W$ we have $\partial(w)=0$, so by the formula in [lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends](2) $D(\iota(g)/w)=\iota(\partial g)/w$ for $g\in A_0[x]$, i.e. on the image of $K_0[x]=W^{-1}A_0[x]$ the derivation $D$ is the image of $d/dx$; in particular $D(f)=\iota(f')$. As $K_0$ has characteristic $0$ and $\deg f\ge1$, $f'
e0$ has degree $<\deg f$, so $f$ irreducible gives $\gcd(f,f')=1$ and $af+bf'=1$ with $a,b\in K_0[x]$; mapping to $R$, the image of $D(f)$ in $R/fR$ is a unit. proof.text:
(Characteristic $p>0$, and conclusion.) Suppose $K_0$ has characteristic $p>0$. Then $A_0
ot\cong\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$: such a ring contains $\Lambda$, a domain which is not a field and whose maximal ideal is generated by a prime number $\ell$, so $\ell
e0$ in $\Lambda$; if $\Lambda$ had characteristic a prime $r$, then $r=\ell$ would give $\ell=0$, and $r
e\ell$ would make $\ell$ a unit ($1=ar+b\ell$ with $a,b\in\mathbf Z$); so $\Lambda$, hence $A_0$ and $K_0$, would have characteristic $0$. Hence (Step 3) there is a ring isomorphism $\sigma:k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0$ for a field $k$, of characteristic $p$ as $k\subseteq K_0$; it extends to $\sigma[x]:k[[X_1,\ldots,X_d]][y]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_0[x]$, $y\mapsto x$. If $\mathfrak r_0=(0)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-helper-g-ring-char-p] with $n=d$, $m=1$ and the prime $\sigma[x]^{-1}(\mathfrak Q_0)$: transported along $\sigma[x]$ (which induces isomorphisms of localizations, completions and fraction fields) it says that $C_0\otimes_{A_0[x]}\kappa((0))$ is geometrically regular over the fraction field $\kappa((0))$ of $A_0[x]$. If $\mathfrak r_0
e(0)$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-another-helper-g-ring] to the Noetherian complete local domain $A_0$ (fraction field of characteristic $p$), $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak Q_0$ (maximal, over $\mathfrak m_0$) and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak r_0$. With Steps 5 and 6, $(\ddagger)$ holds in all cases; hence $(\dagger)$ by Step 3, hence by Step 2 every $C\otimes_{S[x]}\kappa(\mathfrak r)$ is geometrically regular, and by Step 1 the map $S[x]_{\mathfrak Q}	o(S[x]_{\mathfrak Q})^\wedge$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

split_report.summary: Read the proof of More on Algebra 07PV (paragraphs 2-5, lines 12596-12639) and the lemmas it uses: 07PN (check-G-ring-easy), 07PP(1) (formal fibre ascent along quasi-finite maps), Algebra 032D, Algebra 07NF (regular-goes-up, smooth ascent), 07NY (completion-regular), 07PR (helper-G-ring), 07PU (another-helper-G-ring), and 07PE/07PF used by 07PU. Tags verified in tags/tags; 07NT (regular-permanence) is used only in paragraph 1 of 07PV (the parent lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring), not here. Statement kept; [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] cited for completeness (content unchanged). Proof in 7 steps: flatness and Noetherian fibres, reduction mod p = r cap S to a complete local domain (the 07PN identity written out with 00MA and 00CT for the ideal pS[x] inside r), passage to the regular subring A_0 by 032D and 07PP(1) (finiteness of A_0[x] -> A[x], maximality of Q_0 and quasi-finiteness written out), regularity of the completion (0AFS, smoothness of R -> R[x], 07NF, 07NY), char 0 with r_0 = 0 (localization), char 0 with r_0 != 0 (agent-written: the source's 'as a localization' sentence is wrong there; the fibre is a localization of the completion modulo an irreducible f, regular by the derivation argument of 07PU with 07PE/07PF), char p by 07PR (m = 1) and 07PU after excluding the Cohen case. Cited the sibling's nodes (07PN not needed as a node: the identity is written out; 0325, 032D, 07PP(1), 0AFS, 07NY, 07PR, 07NF) and the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth. New unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-another-helper-g-ring (07PU), lem-weil-pbc-derivation-extends (07PE (1)(2)), lem-weil-pbc-hypersurface-derivation-regular (07PF); none in Mathlib (LeanSearch, LeanFinder/Loogle, grep).
